cards.front: Distinguish between transverse and longitudinal waves, with an example of each.
cards.back: In a transverse wave the oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of energy travel, such as electromagnetic waves. In a longitudinal wave they are parallel, such as sound, and the wave shows compressions and rarefactions.

keyPoints.text: transverse: oscillations perpendicular to energy transfer
longitudinal: oscillations parallel to energy transfer

cards.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarised, which is the standard experimental test for the difference.

cards.front: Define the frequency of a wave and give its unit.
cards.back: The number of complete oscillations passing a point per unit time, measured in hertz.

keyPoints.text: number of complete oscillations per unit time

cards.front: Write the wave equation linking speed, frequency and wavelength.

synonyms: wave speed equals frequency times wavelength

cards.explanation: Speed is distance per time, and one wavelength passes per period, so c = lambda / T = f lambda.

cards.front: What condition must two waves satisfy to give a stable interference pattern?
cards.back: They must be coherent: the same frequency and wavelength, with a constant phase difference.

mcq.correct: They must be coherent: the same frequency and wavelength, with a constant phase difference.
distractors: They must have the same amplitude
They must be travelling in the same direction

cards.explanation: If the phase difference drifts, the positions of the maxima move and the pattern blurs out. Equal amplitudes only make the cancellation complete, they are not required for a pattern.

cards.front: State the path difference, in wavelengths, for constructive and for destructive interference.
cards.back: Constructive when the path difference is a whole number of wavelengths, n lambda. Destructive when it is a half-integer number, (n + 1/2) lambda.
cards.explanation: A whole-number difference means the waves arrive in phase; an extra half wavelength puts a crest against a trough.
